title: Iran says its drones hit US base in Kuwait; army chief warns of response 'without geographical restrictions'
dek: Kuwait says it responded to hostile drones as Iran retaliates for the US strike on Qeshm Island; an ADNOC-managed tanker is hit off Oman with 11 crew injured and one missing.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Iran's army said on Wednesday that its drones had attacked US forces at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, its first reported strike on Kuwait since September, and its army chief warned Washington that Iran would respond "more forcefully and without geographical restrictions" if the United States attacked again, according to reports. Kuwait's military said its air defences had responded to hostile drones but did not say where they came from or report any damage.

The attack, which Iranian media described as retaliation for Tuesday's US strike on a Revolutionary Guards missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island, came as a second tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz in two days. The UAE's state-owned shipping company ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels had been attacked while transiting the strait on Tuesday evening, that 11 crew members were injured and that one was unaccounted for.

## What each side says

The Iranian army said its drones targeted US Patriot air-defence systems and drone and missile launch pads at the base, according to Iranian state media. There has been no independent confirmation of any damage. Kuwait's foreign ministry condemned the attacks, saying they "threatened the country's security and stability", and said Kuwait reserved the right to take necessary measures, according to reports. Saudi Arabia also condemned the attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and called for an end to hostilities, reports said.

Bahrain reported fresh Iranian aerial attacks early on Wednesday, issued shelter alerts and later gave the all-clear; its military said it had intercepted several attacks but gave no details of damage. US Central Command has said every Iranian drone launched at Bahrain on Tuesday was intercepted. Iran's army chief, Major General Amir Hatami, warned the US against what he called a "miscalculation", according to Iranian state media.

Separately, a Saudi-led coalition spokesperson said Saudi air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile fired by Yemen's Houthis at Riyadh, reports said.

## The tanker attack

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, run by the Royal Navy, reported that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman on Tuesday evening, starting a fire that was later put out, and that the crew had been evacuated. Industry reports identified the ship as the Navig8 Messi, a tanker commercially managed by ADNOC Logistics & Services. ADNOC did not say who attacked the ship or give the nationalities of the crew.

It was the second attack on a merchant ship in the strait this week. On Monday the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas was hit; India's Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday that 21 of the 24 Indian nationals on board had been brought ashore at Khasab, two were in hospital and one was missing. There was no reported news of the missing Indian sailor by Wednesday evening.

## Background

The United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, killing several senior Iranian leaders including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Talks have stalled despite a memorandum of understanding signed in June, and the US says it is enforcing a naval blockade of Iran's ports on the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday to discuss proposals to narrow differences between Tehran and Washington, Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said, according to reports.

Iran had resumed attacks on US facilities in Bahrain this week after about two months without such incidents. For India, which imports much of its oil and gas through the strait and whose seafarers have been caught up in the attacks, each new round raises the risks for crews and the cost of shipping.

## What happens next

The war is expected to be discussed when US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Iran said on Monday that a regional bloc backed its two-day plan to reopen the strait; Washington has not publicly responded.
